notes: Names printed without a suffix (ALFRED, DRAPER, COOK) are written with 'Street' (the Milling Machine Co. text gives '2529-2541 Cook St.'). Cook jogs at Alfred: the piece north of Alfred (from sheets 254/255, lines 2420/2736 at Alfred's north line) and the piece south of Alfred (lines 2586/2878 at Alfred's south line) have centrelines ~52 px apart at Alfred's centre, so two T points; the north piece is named 'Cook Street (north of Alfred)'. Cook ends at Draper (T; the south side of Draper is continuous). Alfred and Draper both end at Colerain (T); the only things east of Colerain are the Jacob Vogel packing house and the Miami Canal. Colerain bends at Alfred (about 19.5 deg off vertical north of it, about 15 deg south of it), so no separate bend point there; between Draper and Queen City it has three angle points (in bends) and narrows from 60' to about 48 ft as drawn at Queen City. Spring Grove/Draper is the middle of the open crossing (Draper is 50' west of Spring Grove, 60' east; centrelines ~40 px apart). Spring Grove/Queen City is not recorded: Queen City's north line is at y~7575 there and its centre (~7757) falls below the paper edge (~7717); Queen City also slants up toward Colerain on this sheet. Two narrow footbridges cross the canal from Colerain's east line (y~4247-4303 and y~5995-6070); they are not streets and are not recorded. 'JACOB VOGEL AND SONS (SEE MARGIN)' printed in Colerain is a building reference, not a street name. Circled figures are grade elevations. No alleys.
